teacherCues: Write .85 on the board and ask: 'How would you say this as a percent?'
Introduce the D2P trick: move the decimal two places right and add a % sign.

discoveryHook.scenario: In a bag of 55 M&M's, 18 are yellow. That's $\frac{18}{55} = .32727...$, or about 32.73%. Decimals and percents are two ways of expressing the same part of a whole.

blocks.title: 1. Converting Decimals to Percents

questions.prompt: To convert a decimal to a percent, move the decimal point ___ places to the right.

confusionCorner.body: Don't forget the % sign! [[imp:A decimal without % is not the same as a percent.]] 0.85 ≠ 0.85%.
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

visuals.title: D2P: Decimal → Percent
visuals.caption: Move decimal two places right. Add % symbol.

formulaCard.formula: Decimal → move decimal two places right → add %
formulaCard.title: D2P Rule

explanation: [[kw:Percent]] means 'per 100'. The symbol % means $\div 100$, so 15% = $\frac{15}{100} = .15$.
To convert a decimal to a percent: [[imp:Move the decimal point two places to the right and add the % symbol.]]
This multiplies the decimal by 100. Add zeros if needed to fill places.
The memory trick: D2P – Decimal to Percent, move the decimal 2 places right.

steps: One decimal place right multiplies by 10; two places multiplies by 100.
Since percent means per 100, multiplying by 100 converts to percent.
examples.title: B – Why two places?
examples.peerPrompt: Think: each move right multiplies by 10.
examples.prompt: Explain to a classmate why moving the decimal two places is the same as multiplying by 100.

visuals.caption: Convert to percent first, then round like a decimal.
visuals.title: Rounding Percents

explanation: After converting to a percent, you may need to round: [[imp:1. Identify the rounding digit. 2. Look right: if ≥5, round up. 3. Drop digits to the right.]]
Example: 32.72727% → hundredth percent is the 2nd decimal place (2). The next digit (7) is ≥5, so round up the 2 to 3 → 32.73%.
Always first get the number into percent form, then round to the required place.

formulaCard.title: Rounding Steps
notes: Rounding to nearest cent uses same steps.
Be careful with decimal places in percents.
formulaCard.formula:
Step 1: Convert to percent.
Step 2: Identify rounding digit.
Step 3: Look right — 5 or more, round up.
Step 4: Drop extra digits.

challengeCorner.prompt: A survey shows 17 out of 23 people prefer tea. What percent is that, to the nearest tenth percent?
hints: Tenth percent = first decimal; next digit is 1, so keep 9: 73.9%.

confusionCorner.title: Watch out!
confusionCorner.body: Always convert the decimal to a percent BEFORE rounding. [[imp:If you round the decimal first, you may get a different percent.]]

discoveryHook.scenario: 18 yellow M&M's out of 55 gives $\frac{18}{55} = 32.72727...\%$. Rounding to the nearest hundredth percent gives 32.73%. Rounding percents follows the same rules as rounding decimals.

blocks.title: 2. Rounding Percents

questions.prompt: To round a percent, look at the digit to the ___ of the rounding place.

hints: Hundredths = second decimal place. The digit is 2, next is 7.
questions.prompt: Round 32.727% to the nearest hundredth percent.
Express $\frac{2}{3}$ as a percent rounded to the nearest tenth percent.
hints: Tenths digit 6, next 6 → round up to 7.

teacherCues: Show the same rounding rules as for decimals.
Walk through an example with a repeating decimal.

examples.prompt: Express $\frac{5}{12}$ as a percent rounded to the nearest tenth percent.
steps: Tenth percent = 1st decimal place (6). Next digit is 6 (≥5).
examples.title: A – Round to nearest tenth percent

examples.prompt: Why does 16.36% round to 16.4% when rounding to the nearest tenth percent?
steps: Tenths digit is 3; hundredths digit is 6.
examples.title: B – Explain rounding up

steps: Whole percent = 87. Look at tenths digit: 5.
examples.prompt: Round 87.561% to the nearest whole percent.
examples.title: C – Round to nearest whole percent

blocks.title: 3. Converting Percents to Decimals

explanation: To convert a percent to a decimal: [[imp:1. Drop the % symbol. 2. Move the decimal point two places to the left (divide by 100).]]
For [[kw:fractional percents]] (like $\frac{1}{5}$%): first convert the fraction to a decimal (e.g., $\frac{1}{5}=0.2$), then move the decimal two places left → 0.002.
Memory trick: P2D – Percent to Decimal, move decimal 2 places left.

formulaCard.formula: Percent → drop % → move decimal two places left
formulaCard.title: P2D Rule
notes: For fractional percents, first convert the fraction to a decimal, then move.

visuals.title: P2D: Percent → Decimal
visuals.caption: Move the decimal two places left; add leading zeros if needed.

discoveryHook.scenario: Zoom laid off 15% of its workforce. As a decimal, that's 0.15. To calculate actual numbers, you must convert percents to decimals by moving the decimal point two places left.

examples.prompt: Explain how to write $\frac{1}{5}$% as a decimal.
examples.title: B – Fractional percent
examples.peerPrompt: First, what is $\frac{1}{5}$ as a decimal?
steps: Because it's less than 1%, you get a very small decimal.

confusionCorner.body: Fractional percents (like $\frac{1}{2}$%) are less than 1%. [[imp:Always convert the fraction to a decimal first, then move the decimal point.]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

teacherCues: Introduce P2D: Percent to Decimal, move decimal two places left.
Show how fractional percents (like 1/5%) are handled.

questions.prompt: To convert a percent to a decimal, move the decimal point two places to the ___.

examples.title: B – Denominator divides 100
steps: This method works when denominator is a factor of 100.

visuals.title: Fraction → Percent
visuals.caption: Divide to get decimal, then move decimal two places right for percent.

explanation: To convert a fraction to a percent: [[imp:1. Divide the numerator by the denominator to get a decimal. 2. Convert the decimal to a percent (D2P).]]
Alternative: If denominator divides evenly into 100, multiply numerator and denominator to make denominator 100.
For mixed numbers: convert to improper fraction or add fraction percent to whole number.

formulaCard.title: Fraction to Percent
notes: For mixed numbers, convert to improper fraction first or add whole number percent.

blocks.title: 4. Converting Fractions to Percents

discoveryHook.scenario: In the M&M's bag, 6 out of 55 are brown. As a percent, that's $\frac{6}{55} \approx 10.91\%$. You can convert a fraction to a percent by dividing numerator by denominator, then converting the decimal to a percent.

teacherCues: Show two methods: divide then move decimal, or make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100.
Emphasize the division method as it works for all fractions.

challengeCorner.prompt: A basketball player makes 18 out of 24 free throws. What is his free throw percentage?

confusionCorner.body: For repeating decimals, round the percent to the desired place. [[imp:Always convert to percent before rounding, not before.]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

questions.prompt: To convert a fraction to a percent, first ___ the numerator by the denominator.

confusionCorner.body: Don't forget to remove the % symbol when writing the fraction. [[imp:25% = 25/100, not 25% / 100.]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

discoveryHook.scenario: If a store discounts an item by 25%, that means $\frac{25}{100}$ or $\frac{1}{4}$ off. To calculate discounts, it's often easier to work with fractions.

challengeCorner.prompt: A stock rose 12.5%. Express this increase as a fraction.
hints: 12.5/100 simplifies to 1/8 after multiplying numerator and denominator by 2.

examples.title: A – Whole number percent
examples.prompt: Convert 60% to a fraction in lowest terms.
Explain why 150% as a fraction is $\frac{3}{2}$ or $1\frac{1}{2}$.
examples.title: B – Percent greater than 100

explanation: To convert a percent to a fraction: [[imp:1. Write the percent as a fraction with denominator 100. 2. Reduce to lowest terms.]]

For fractional percents (like $\frac{1}{2}$%): first write as $\frac{1/2}{100}$, then simplify: multiply numerator by the reciprocal: $\frac{1}{2} \div 100 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{100} = \frac{1}{200}$.
Mixed number percents: convert to improper fraction first, then write over 100 and simplify.

visuals.title: Percent → Fraction
visuals.caption: Percent means 'per 100'; put it over 100 and simplify.

questions.prompt: To convert a percent to a fraction, write the percent over ___ and reduce.
Write 20% as a fraction in lowest terms.

hints: Multiply numerator and denominator by 10, then simplify.

blocks.title: 5. Converting Percents to Fractions
teacherCues: Demonstrate: write percent over 100, then reduce.
For fractional percents, handle the fraction first.
